recommendations: Admit high-risk ACS patients, including all STEMI patients, to a CCU/ICCU after reperfusion.
ECG monitoring for arrhythmias and ST-segment changes is recommended for at least 24 h after symptom onset in all high-risk ACS patients.
Hospitals caring for high-risk ACS patients should have an ICCU/CCU able to manage ischaemia, severe HF, arrhythmias and common comorbidities.
Determine LVEF before hospital discharge in all patients with ACS.
Discharge of high-risk ACS patients within 48–72 h may be considered in selected patients if early rehabilitation and adequate follow-up are arranged.
Routine radial access and use of DES are the standard of care during PCI for ACS.
Intravascular imaging should be considered to guide PCI and may be considered in patients with ambiguous culprit lesions.
Routine thrombus aspiration is not recommended.
CABG should be considered in patients with an occluded IRA when PCI is not feasible or unsuccessful and there is a large area of myocardium in jeopardy.
In SCAD, PCI is recommended only for patients with symptoms and signs of ongoing myocardial ischaemia, a large area of myocardium in jeopardy, and reduced antegrade flow.

principles: Base revascularisation strategy (IRA PCI, multivessel PCI/CABG) on the patient's clinical status, comorbidities and disease complexity.
For patients with MVD presenting with cardiogenic shock (CS), IRA-only PCI during the index procedure is recommended.
For patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI, complete revascularisation is recommended either during the index PCI or within 45 days.
For patients presenting with NSTE-ACS and MVD, complete revascularisation should be considered, preferably during the index procedure.
For STEMI, decisions regarding PCI of non-IRA are based on angiographic severity; for NSTE-ACS, functional invasive evaluation of non-IRA severity during the index procedure may be considered.

MINOCA.definition: Patients present with symptoms suggestive of ACS, demonstrate troponin elevation and have non-obstructive coronary arteries at angiography (i.e. coronary artery stenosis <50% in any major epicardial vessel).
MINOCA.epidemiology: Found in approximately 1–14% of patients with ACS.
recommendations: Consider MINOCA as a working diagnosis encompassing a heterogeneous group of underlying causes (cardiac and extra-cardiac).
Follow a diagnostic algorithm to determine the underlying cause in patients with an initial working diagnosis of MINOCA.
CMR imaging is a key diagnostic tool in patients with a working diagnosis of MINOCA.
